To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
response rates decrease and postreinforcer pauses increase with time on interval schedules of reinforcement, and that these effects are more pronounced on interval schedules than on ratio schedules.
response persistence under interval schedules of food reinforcement is greater than that under ratio schedules of food reinforcement.

responding maintained by progressive-ratio schedules is more sensitive than responding maintained by yoked-interval (equivalent interresponse time) schedules to changes in response cost and reinforcement magnitude, and that the ratio and interval schedules control different response distributions in time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the strength of operant behavior and its resistance to change, and with the factors affecting this relationship.
the relationship between response strength and the persistence of response rate under ratio and interval schedules of reinforcement.
the relationship between the temporal pattern of behavior and its persistence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the yoked-intervals schedule was more persistent than the yoked-ratio schedule.
ratio schedules are more sensitive to response deprivation than interval schedules, and that the difference between the two types of schedules is not a simple function of response deprivation.

ratio and interval schedules of reinforcement differ in the degree to which response strength and persistence are affected by the ratio of responses to reinforcers, but that the differences are not as large as they are sometimes made to appear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ratio reinforcement schedules produce a stronger response than do interval schedules, and the response strength produced by the ratio schedule is more persistent than the response strength produced under interval reinforcement schedules.
the ratio-interval distinction is a very useful way to organize our thinking about behavior.
response persistence is a function of reinforcement history and the response requirements of the schedule of reinforcement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the yoked-intervals procedure is an excellent way to study response persistence under different schedules of reinforcement.
response strength is not a unitary phenomenon.
response strength is not always the best predictor of behavioral persistence.
